Fact.Name: The accrued annual leave payout inside the W-2 disability amount
Fact.Description: SCREEN. Question: "Did the amount you just entered include a lump sum payment for accrued annual leave, and if so how much?" Help text: if you retire on disability, a lump sum payment for accrued annual leave is a SALARY payment, not disability income. It pays you for leave you earned while you were working, not for the time you are absent from work because of your disability, so it does not count for the credit for the elderly or the disabled even though your employer reports it on the same Form W-2. Enter the leave payout part of the amount on the previous screen; leave this blank, or enter $0, if none of it was accrued leave. Asked when: the filer is retired on permanent and total disability and has answered ../writableTotalTaxableDisabilityAmount. Unanswered posture: DEFAULTED to $0, and the reason is the previous screen. ../writableTotalTaxableDisabilityAmount already asks for the amount paid "as wages (or in place of wages) while you were absent from work on account of your permanent and total disability", so a filer who followed that instruction has already left the leave payout out; this box DECOMPOSES an attestation that is already scoped rather than collecting a new unscoped quantity, and $0 here means "nothing bundled". An Incomplete default is not available: the whole of Schedule R Part III hangs off ../totalTaxableDisabilityAmount, so a blank on this box would put line 11, line 12 and the credit Incomplete on every return in the population, including the five committed upstream scenarios that answer the amount and never see this question. THE RESIDUAL RISK IS A SCREEN ORDER RISK, not a graph risk: the carve out bites only where the screen is not shown, so this question has to be asked of every filer who answers the amount. Validation: Dollar, Min $0, ONE amount per filer. NO UPPER BOUND AGAINST THE DISABILITY AMOUNT, the disclosed-not-repaired posture the sibling intakes take: an entry above it is ACCEPTED and the exclusion it produces is capped at the amount rather than refused, so line 11 floors at $0 and never turns negative. What the answer feeds: ../accruedAnnualLeavePayoutExcludedFromDisabilityIncome, subtracted from the W-2 leg of ../totalTaxableDisabilityAmount before it reaches Schedule R line 11.

Fact.Name: Schedule R line 13a, nontaxable social security and railroad benefits
Fact.Description: 1040 Schedule R line 13a: Nontaxable social security and railroad benefits. Two legs add: socialSecurity:/nonTaxableSocialSecurityBenefits (Form 1040 line 6a minus 6b, the ordinary nontaxable portion) PLUS the collection of terrorist-attack disability exclusions (IRC 104(a)(5)) already subtracted before line 6a is formed (socialSecurity:/socialSecurityBenefits). §22(c)(3)(A)(i)(I) reaches "amounts received ... which is excluded from gross income and payable under ... title II of the Social Security Act", with the only carve-out (the flush sentence, "no reduction shall be made under clause (i)(III) for any amount described in section 104(a)(4)") reaching clause (i)(III) (VA-administered law) and section 104(a)(4) (combat-related injury), not clause (i)(I) or section 104(a)(5) (terrorist-attack injury). A title II SSDI amount excluded under 104(a)(5) is therefore within clause (i)(I) and belongs on line 13a; without the second leg it never reached this line, because 6a minus 6b removes only the TAXABLE/NONTAXABLE split of what was reported, not an amount already excluded before 6a was formed.

Do NOT include on this line any pension, annuity, or similar allowance for personal injuries or sickness resulting from active service in the armed forces of any country, or in the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration or the Public Health Service, and do NOT include a disability annuity payable under section 808 of the Foreign Service Act of 1980 — none of those amounts reduce this credit. CORRECTED. THE SECOND ADDEND IS GONE. Until this change the body was Add(/edcSelfReportedNonTaxablePaymentAmount, income:/nonTaxablePensionsAndAnnuities), and that second term is Form 1040 line 5a less line 5b, i.e. the IRC 72(b) exclusion ratio, which its own authority comment in income.xml names as such ("Gross income does not include that part of any amount received as an annuity ... which bears the same ratio to such amount as the investment in the contract bears to the expected return"). THE PRINTED LINE EXCLUDES EXACTLY THAT QUANTITY, TWICE OVER. 2025 Instructions for Schedule R, Line 13b (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sr.pdf, page 4, RIGHT column of a two column extraction): the line takes "Veterans' pensions (but not military disability pensions)" and "Any other pension, annuity, or disability benefit that is excluded from income under any provision of federal law other than the Internal Revenue Code", and then says in the same breath "Don't include amounts that are treated as a return of your cost of a pension or annuity." Basis recovery under section 72(b) IS a return of cost, and section 72 IS the Internal Revenue Code, so the old addend failed both halves of the printed test. The statute says the same: IRC 22(c)(3)(A)(ii) reduces only by amounts "excluded from gross income under any provision of law NOT CONTAINED IN THIS TITLE" (26 U.S.C. 22, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section22&num=0&edition=2024), and title 26 is the Internal Revenue Code.
THE IRS'S OWN WORKED EXAMPLE CORROBORATES IT. Instructions for Schedule R, Examples, Example 1 (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sr.pdf, page 5): Jesse has a $15,900 taxable disability pension and $700 of nontaxable social security, and line 13c is $700 - the pension contributes nothing to the reduction. Example 2 (lines 341-351, tabulated at 300-316) is the same shape. NEITHER PRINTED EXAMPLE CARRIES A NONZERO 13b, so no IRS worked example pins the 13b limb itself; the two examples pin the ABSENCE this correction restores.
WHAT REMAINS ON THIS LINE is /edcSelfReportedNonTaxablePaymentAmount alone - the taxpayer attested veterans' and other non-title-26 exclusions, which is precisely the class 22(c)(3)(A)(i)(III) and (ii) describe and the only class this dictionary can source. No 1099-R quantity belongs here: every nontaxable component the 1099-R model can produce (72(b) basis recovery, a 402(c) rollover, the 402(l) public safety officer exclusion) is an exclusion granted BY title 26.
THE BUG THIS CLOSES, and why a floor would have hidden it. This fact was measured NEGATIVE - minus 18,000 on one committed return and minus 30,000 on another - because a fully taxable pension leaves line 5a blank by the Form 1040 instruction while line 5b carries the whole figure, so 5a less 5b is minus 5b. The proposed fix was max(5a - 5b, 0). THAT FIX IS REFUTED BY THE SOURCES ABOVE: it would have left the POSITIVE half of the same class on the line, which is 6,000 on node-test elderlyAndDisabled/schedule-r-line13b-excludes-return-of-cost and up to 41,864 on scenarios/spine/1040-withholdings-without-attachments.tsv - a partly taxable pension's return of cost, named in the printed instruction as the thing not to include. The negative was a symptom of a wrong DECOMPOSITION, not of a missing floor.
VALUES THAT MOVE, all on the committed corpus and all corrections: 24 spine rows carry a nonzero value for this fact today and every one of them becomes $0. Nineteen are positive (200.00 on eight ats/ticket 1099-R rows; 2,200.00 on three savers rows; 6,200.00 on three; 8,000.00 on three; 10,000.00 on ats-3-1099r; 41,864.00 on 1040-withholdings-without-attachments) and carry line 13c (/edcTotalNonTaxableAmount) with them to $0; five are negative (minus 10,000.00 on one, minus 18,000.00 on two and minus 30,000.00 on two) and leave 13c at $0 where the existing floor already put it. NO TAX MOVES ANYWHERE: /netEdcAmount is 0.00 on all 24. The one committed scenario with a live credit, scenarios/spine/edc-ats-1.tsv (13b 425.00, 13c 425.00, /netEdcAmount 686.00), is NOT a mover - its 425 is entirely /writableEdcSelfReportedNonTaxablePaymentAmount, it carries no 1099-R at all, and it is byte identical after this change.

1040 Schedule R line 16: the AGI the section 22 credit's income limit is measured on. **PLAIN AGI, with NO section 931/933 add-back — and that is SOURCED, not incidental.**
⚠⚠ A TAXPAYER-FAVOURABLE RESIDUAL WAS ONCE DECLARED HERE AND IS WITHDRAWN. The reasoning was: Publication 1321 cautions that "Excluded Puerto Rico source income must be included in gross income when calculating income limits for certain credits", and section 22 is a credit with an income limit, so the caution reads onto it. **IRC 22 was vendored to settle that, and it does not.**
TWO INDEPENDENT REASONS FROM THE PRINTED STATUTE, either one sufficient: 1. SECTION 22 NAMES PLAIN AGI AND NO EXCLUSION SECTION AT ALL. Section 22(d): "If the adjusted gross income of the taxpayer exceeds- (1) $7,500 ... the section 22 amount shall be reduced by one-half of the excess". Sections 911, 931 and 933 appear NOWHERE in section 22. That is the same test that correctly leaves scheduleE /section8582Magi (section 469(i)(3)(E) names no exclusion section), taxCalculations /magiForIraDeduction (section 219(g)(3) names 135/137/221/911, not 931/933) and form8960 /niitMagi (section 1411(d) names 911 alone) on plain AGI. The earlier MAGI walk classified all four together and was right about all four. 2. SECTION 22'S OTHER REDUCTION LIMB EXCLUDES THIS INCOME BY ITS OWN TERMS. Section 22(c)(3)(A)(ii) reduces the section 22 amount by a pension, annuity or disability benefit "which is excluded from gross income under any provision of law NOT CONTAINED IN THIS TITLE". Section 933 IS contained in this title, so it is outside that clause. Both of section 22's reduction mechanisms leave a section 933 exclusion alone.
AND PUBLICATION 1321 DOES NOT REACH IT EITHER — the word doing the work is "certain". Its CREDITS section enumerates exactly four credits: the American Opportunity Tax Credit, the Foreign Tax Credit, the Child Tax Credit and the Earned Income Tax Credit (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p1321.pdf, page 7). The credit for the elderly and the permanently and totally disabled is NOT among them. A general caution plus an enumeration that omits this credit is not authority for wiring it.
SO 28,174 IS THE CORRECT VALUE and the node test pins it as correct rather than as a disclosed defect. The knockout's condition (A) is NOT re-opened on this surface.
WHAT THE EPISODE IS WORTH KEEPING FOR: that earlier walk recorded this surface as "plain AGI, needs no wiring" — the right answer for a reason stated about PLUMBING rather than statute, which is why it looked fragile the moment the plumbing moved and why a later change believed it had broken something. An exemption justified by what a fact happens to read is only as durable as what it reads; an exemption justified by what the statute says survives. Three of that walk's four exemptions were statutory and never wobbled.
